findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the fix reconciles marker.py's blocking LOCK_EX-on-a-file-object with lock_kernel's non-blocking take_exclusive(fd): either specify the deadline/poll loop and fd handling that preserves blocking serialization (AC3), or justify the local `if fcntl is not None` guard as the approach that keeps marker's existing semantics with smaller blast radius.
evidence: lock.py:196-224 _acquire_fcntl uses _kernel.take_exclusive(fd) which is fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) — non-blocking, polled to a deadline
marker.py:31-38 opens `with open(lock_path,'a') as lock_fd` then `fcntl.flock(lock_fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)` — a BLOCKING acquire on a file object, released with fcntl.LOCK_UN in finally
AC3: 'Serialization is still enforced on POSIX (the existing behaviour is unchanged when fcntl is available)' — a non-blocking helper changes the wait behaviour
S1 comment: fsutil case was explicitly noted as needing 'a blocking take this selector does not expose' — the same mismatch applies to marker.py's blocking LOCK_EX
findings.finding: The plan directs reuse of S1's guarded exclusive-lock helper (lock_kernel.take_exclusive) but does not reconcile that helper's semantics with marker.py's: lock_kernel's POSIX leg is fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) — a NON-blocking take on an OS-level fd that callers must poll to a deadline — whereas write_marker/remove_marker currently hold a BLOCKING fcntl.flock(lock_fd, LOCK_EX) on a Python file object (open(lock_path,'a')) and release via fcntl.LOCK_UN. Adopting the helper as-is would either change acquisition from blocking-wait to non-blocking (a behaviour change AC3 says must not happen) or require an added poll/deadline loop the plan does not describe, and would change the fd type and the unlock call. The mechanism is therefore under-specified where it matters most.
findings.location: 'Sequence after S1' / 'reuse whatever guarded exclusive-lock helper S1 lands' and AC3
scenarios: Two concurrent archivers contend on the same ticket's .write.lock on POSIX: today one blocks until the other releases; a non-blocking take would immediately fail/return and could skip serialization or spin
Implementer wires marker to take_exclusive(fd) but marker holds a file object, not an fd — a type/lifecycle mismatch surfaces at integration
